MGXD · Fall 2026 Symposium · Service design

Nobody can see why.

How engineers actually work with agentic AI
ThesisThe bottleneck moved from writing code to establishing intent.
A seven-week service design study, and one response to what it found.
→
Then Vibe coding Prompt, accept, ship. The agent writes, the engineer moves on. The code is the only record.
Now Spec-driven development The spec sets intent, the agent builds against it, and the engineer reviews what it built. The spec is the source of truth.
The gap Nobody has designed the human experience of working this way yet.
P1 Backend engineering lead Main company The spec is the source of truth
P2 Frontend engineer Main company The Show-Me Builder
P3 DevOps engineer Main company Has to prove the process ran
P4 Engineering leader Outside comparison Spends attention where the risk is
CaveatThree from one company, one outside comparison, mostly heavy AI users.
Problem statement

Engineers working with AI agents need a way to pass on the reasoning behind their decisions, not just the finished code, because once work leaves their hands, reviewers, QA, and the next engineer can’t tell a deliberate choice from a guess.

01 How might we help the next person understand why a decision was made without having to ask the person who made it?
02 How might we make it obvious to everyone on a ticket what “correct” means before work starts?
03 How might we help engineers see where the agent guessed, before that guess ships?
Frontend engineer
As a frontend engineer, I want the expected behavior written down before I start.
Senior backend engineer
As a senior backend engineer, I want to see where the agent guessed.
Engineering leader
As an engineering leader, I want review effort to scale with risk,

A record the agent writes as a byproduct of building, structured like the spec, that captures every judgment call the engineer makes in a gap and every inference the agent makes on its own.

It persists above the session, ranks decisions by risk, must be checked before push, and is acknowledged at handoff.

Seven design decisions
1Captured as a byproduct2Two kinds of entry3Structured like the spec4Lives above the session5Checked before push6Questions to the owner7Acknowledged at handoff
01 The ledger fills as the agent builds Every guess is marked inferred, every judgment call is the engineer’s. Nobody fills a form.
02 Filter the code by decision Agentic assumptions, gaps or user decisions, each line explained in plain language.
03 Ask the owner from the code A drafted question with a preview attached. The answer lands on the entry.
04 Proceed with stated risk No answer yet? Go ahead on purpose. The reviewer sees the reason first.
05 Push with reasons A check ranked by risk. The signed ledger goes to review with the diff.
“

The ledger doesn’t make engineers faster. It makes their decisions visible to everyone who comes after them.

Thank you
